questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] A client has fine white flakes and little redness. What is the most measured first step at the chair?
options: Name a medical diagnosis and start a treatment plan
Describe what you can see, ask what they have noticed, and suggest a gentle over-the-counter approach if appropriate
Tell them it is definitely psoriasis
Refuse to comment on anything you see
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Stylists observe and guide; they do not diagnose. Replace with Marketing's final copy.

questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Which sign is more likely to need a calm specialist referral than a product swap alone?
options: Occasional dry flakes with a comfortable scalp
A small amount of product build-up at the crown
Red, spreading, or painful change on the scalp
Hair that feels drier after a holiday
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Red, spreading, or painful change sits outside routine salon product advice.

questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] A client mentions sudden smooth, round patches of loss. What stays inside a stylist's scope?
options: Diagnose alopecia areata and predict regrowth
Document what you observe in neutral language and recommend specialist assessment
Apply a strong scalp peel to stimulate growth
Reassure them it cannot be anything medical
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Observe, document, refer. Do not diagnose.

questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Which opening keeps the client in control of a sensitive scalp conversation?
options: You're losing your hair.
I've noticed a change here — have you noticed anything?
You have a medical condition.
I will not mention anything I see.
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Observation plus permission is safer than a verdict.

questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] How should you frame a referral so it sounds like support rather than alarm?
options: I cannot help you.
This is serious — see a doctor immediately.
A trichologist or GP can give you a clearer picture of what is going on.
This is beyond anyone in a salon, so there is nothing to do.
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Referral as a positive next step protects trust.

questions.questionText: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] A client becomes tearful while talking about shedding. What is the most professional next move?
options: Change the subject quickly
Tell them not to worry and that it will grow back
Acknowledge the feeling, give a little space, and stay steady
Diagnose the cause so they feel better
questions.explanation: [DRAFT PLACEHOLDER] Acknowledge emotion; do not minimise or diagnose.
